SCOPE NOTE on the correction above, so it is not read as broader than it is.

My third comment corrects the mechanism stated in my SECOND comment — "four pytest-xdist workers ... the suite exhausts its own semaphore" — and nothing else. It does NOT correct this ticket's overall framing.

My FIRST comment already framed the cause cross-session ("Four slots, more than four consumers", naming another session's worktree by name), and AC4 already asked for exactly the slot-holder inventory that the host-global finding supplies. So a reader should not conclude that this ticket was wrong about the shape of the problem; it was right, and the second comment narrowed it in a way the third undoes.

What the host-global finding genuinely ADDS, over what this ticket already said:
- the concrete code path (`gate_admission._slot_dir()` -> `store_root()/locks` -> `tempfile.gettempdir()`);
- the scale — 31 tests across 9 files, not the single test originally filed;
- why ordinary triage misleads: re-running in isolation does not isolate, because the slot directory is outside the test session's control.

Recording this because I asked an implementing agent to write "this supersedes 9c2e's mechanism" into its own ticket, and it declined on the grounds that the record did not support the claim. It re-read this ticket, told me to do the same, and was correct. I withdrew the request. The detailed follow-up is filed as `stuffed-energistic-ladybird` (`846b-4b51-0254-48fd`), linked `relates_to`, and is positioned as the ANSWER to AC4 rather than a correction of it — which is the accurate relationship.
